plan-the-economic-model-rebuilt-on-the-d.text: Plan: the economic model, rebuilt on the decided design.

This page plans the Lean work that runs after slice three: the whole economic design stated in the model, the thirteen statements the design allows the paper to make, and the controls that keep each of them honest. The paper itself waits until this work is done. Planning only: no model work starts before this plan is cleared. It replaces the earlier plan, whose bond, split, booking root and termination fee no longer exist.

story.text: As the operator reading one page, I learn which statements the model will prove, in which slice, which scenario guards each one, and which choices the plan still needs from me, so that I can clear the plan or return a line before anyone writes a proof.

what-the-model-has-and-what-the-design-a.text: What the model has, and what the design adds.

The model lacks, and the slices add: output references and a set of unspent outputs; reference inputs beside spent inputs; a validity interval, a ledger fee and a donation on a transaction; the registration cost, minimum tip and maximum booking width; a pending-request pool and booking steps (today a request is an argument, not a state); the registration and the termination request with their exact contents; the treasury as a recipient. Registration is the edge insertActive and termination the edge updateTerminal; the five refused edges stay refused.

names.text: The operator agreed these names on 14 October 2026; the plan and the model use them from slice six on. Declarations that already exist keep their names until a slice restates them.

The syntax tag's minting checks only that the tags are present, never the application's rule: for a registration the application tag; for a termination the singular tag and the application tag. The syntax tag and the application tag share one life: both are minted at booking and burned by every exit, never returned, so there is no tag without a pending request and no pending request without its tags. The tag policies allow a burn with no condition; the exit rules are the request validator's spend.

the-statements.text: Numbers are those of the design's list of what the paper may state. Names are planned and live in Singular.Statements. A statement is to prove until a Lean declaration with only the standard axioms exists. Every statement quantifies over accepted transactions in reachable worlds, never over what a builder produces.

Supporting statements, each in the slice that needs it: reference_inputs_not_consumed (with the premise disjointInputs), spent_reference_refused, overlapping_reference_is_spent, balanced_transaction_creates_no_value, zero_donation_omits_field (five, proved); booked_request_has_exact_contents, booked_time_is_interval_end, booked_time_not_before_inclusion, booking_width_within_limit (six); world_supply_sync, termination_request_carries_genuine_token (seven); rejection_batch_members_distinct, sweep_leaves_pool_untouched (eight); refunds_sum_per_address (nine); fold_routes_every_amount, tag_supplies_equal_pending (ten). Statement 4 rests on booked_time_not_before_inclusion: the booked time is the upper end of the interval the booking transaction was valid in, so expiry comes no earlier than both windows after the booking was included.

the-slices.text: Each slice starts with its failing controls, committed first and failing for the intended reason on the branch as it stands, then the model, the statements, the corpus rows, and the regeneration of every copy the change moves (corpora, register and digests, theorem page, simulator mirror, application corpus, coverage record, restatement table). The driver protocol version moves in the first slice that changes a declared question. A slice ends with the list of its statements and their axiom lines (see "Names and receipts"). One writer per slice; a slice that runs for four hours is cut again.

Five: parameters and the transaction vocabulary. *As a registry creator, I fix the three parameters once and see every fold leave them as they were; as a reviewer, I read a transaction as the ledger shows it.* Adds the three parameters (default zero in old input, preserved by folds, the maximum booking width below the processing window); output references and the unspent set; reference inputs; the validity interval, fee and donation on a transaction (a zero donation omits the field); the exact state token identity (policy and name); the balance relation. Statement 1 and the five supporting statements. Controls: a fold that changes a parameter; a spent reference; an unbalanced transaction. The registry's expected state token is the pair (registry identity, name zero): an abstraction, stated as such, that keeps the check exact for every pair an output presents.

Five-b: review and improvement of the Lean base. *As the author of slices six to ten, and of the paper, I build on a base whose names say what they mean and whose modules are small and cohesive.* Inserted by the operator's direction before slice six. A bounded review of the whole lean/ tree (about 8,400 lines; five modules over 700 lines) in at most seven checkpoints: a written review ranked by what each finding costs slices six to ten; the tools that read the model by file learn to read a set of modules; the large modules are split into cohesive submodules, each split a move with no change of meaning; at most two batches of renames and structural improvements. No statement is weakened and no meaning changes; the qualified names of protected and paper-cited statements stay; renaming a declaration that main already has, and any finding that needs a ruling, is listed and not applied. Writer Codex gpt-6-astra at medium effort, auditor Grok. No new statement and no new control; the written forms and the corpora of scenarios stay byte-identical.

Six: registrations. *As a requester, I book a registration holding exactly the registration cost, a tip of at least the minimum, the carrier ada and the application tag, and my booked time cannot be moved.* Adds the pending-request pool and the booking step into it, the registration request, the exact-contents rule (declared tip apart from held value), the syntax tag with its provenance (a request is pending only if a booking made it), and the booking rule: the interval is at most the maximum width wide and the booked time is its upper end. The syntax tag and the application tag are minted at booking with the pending request. The mint validator stays with ticket 529; this slice models what the syntax tag guarantees. The four supporting statements. Controls: a dirty request, hidden surplus, a forged syntax tag, a backdated booking, a booking wider than the maximum.

Seven: terminations. *As an application, I release a key's singular tag into a termination request with my application tag; as anyone, I see at most one termination pending per key and the supply still adds up.* Adds the termination request (token, tip, carrier ada, application tag; no refund address, no time), its booking step (the token moves from the application's custody into the request) and the supply laws counting tokens held by pending requests. Statement 9 and the two supporting statements. Controls: a forged singular tag or application tag, a second termination of one key, a termination whose token is not in custody.

Eight: rejection reads the state. *As a processor, I reject mismatching or expired registrations in one batch against the state output I read but do not spend.* Adds the accepted-rejection judgement over a transaction: the state output referenced with the exact token and read for its root, no state output spent, distinct request inputs, one interval, each member admitted on a current mismatch or on expiry, terminations never admitted; each rejected request's syntax tag and application tag burned; the rejection arm leaves the fold. The request address has two spending arms: an output lacking either tag is not a request and anyone may spend it, a tagged output leaves only through an exit that burns its tags. Restates slices two and three. Statements 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8 and two supporting statements. Controls: the old state-spending path, a fake, foreign or stale state, an overlapping state spend, a live member inside a batch, a repeated input, a tagged request spent through the sweep arm, a rejection that carries a tag out alive.

Nine: refunds. *As a requester, I get back everything but the tip when my request is rejected and everything when I retract; as a refund address in a batch, I get exactly my sum.* Adds the refund obligations of rejection and retraction for the new contents, in lovelace and summed per refund address, the return of the registration cost, and the burn of both tags by retraction. Statement 6, the second half of statement 7 and one supporting statement. Controls: a reused refund, a refund short of held minus tip, a retraction that carries a tag out alive.

Ten: folds. *As the treasury, I receive at least the registration cost for each key registered and everything but the tip of each terminated key; as a requester with a booked termination, I see it can always be folded.* Adds the fold of a registration (the processing window; routing of the cost, tip and carrier) and of a termination (no window; the singular tag, the syntax tag and the application tag burned; everything but the tip donated), the tag flow of both folds (a registration fold burns the syntax tag and the application tag and mints the singular tag at the destination), the donation floor and the processors' take. Statements 7 (first half), 10, 11 and 12 and two supporting statements. Controls: a termination stranded by a check made at fold time, one donation counted for many keys, a forged application tag, an unbalanced fold, a fold that carries a tag out alive.

controls.text: A control is a scenario the model must refuse, or a variant of the model for which a statement must fail. Each is kept as corpus rows that are refused for the intended reason (the wrong-reason control applies), and, where it is a variant, as a Lean example. The slice of each is above. Two controls recur in every slice that has exits: a tagged request cannot be spent through the sweep arm, and an exit that spends a request without burning its tags (a tag carried out alive) is refused.

decisions-taken.text: The old fee pin and the new minimum tip. The state already carries a pinned maxFee, read by the existing tip-cover lemma. The design adds a minimum tip. Both are kept: the minimum tip is a new pinned number checked at booking and the fee pin behaves as it did. No statement assumes a relation between them; the relation is an open item, settled when the validators are made to agree with the model.

Slice four is withdrawn. The design takes rejection out of the fold's action list: a rejection never spends the state output and never shares a transaction with a fold, so no batch holds both and the story of slice four cannot be told. Statement 3 (a rejection ordered before a fold cannot invalidate it) carries the protection, in slice eight.

open-items-kept-open.text: The items of the design that remain open, and one the plan found. The fate of a registration's application tag on a successful fold is decided: it is burned, never returned, so no restitution output exists.

the-design-page-and-the-paper.text: The design page and the paper.

The design page is the decided design, committed with this plan. The paper starts only when this Lean work is done, so that it can refer to the model: a fresh writer, briefed from the finished model and the design page. Until then every statement is a plan, not a claim.

Names and receipts. Every statement above is declared as a theorem in Singular.Statements, the namespace the compiled axiom gate walks, so its fully qualified name is Singular.Statements.<planned name> and a build that passes proves it uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Each slice ends with a list of its new statements, each with its fully qualified name, the AXIOMS line that #audit_statements report prints for it, and the revision it was printed at; the regenerated theorem register and theorem page carry the same names and digests. A definition the paper cites (for example onlyRootChanged) is cited by its qualified name at the same revision. The paper's brief requires each economic statement to name its declaration by qualified name, exact revision and axiom line, and marks nothing proved unless that declaration exists and the gate passed on it.

staffing-and-gate.text: The Lean writer is Codex gpt-6-astra at high effort, the persistent auditor Grok, as for every slice. The gate version 4 maps the existing commands onto these slices. The files are in the touch list, section "Slices five to ten"; the modules, data and functions in the model rows.
